verdicts.evidence: The ST-vs-OR synthetic experiment (n=4000, 8 reps, 3 censoring mechanisms × 4 rates) produces concrete bias numbers showing IBS is strongly mechanism-dependent (admin −0.0795 vs cov-dep 0.0000 at 80%) while C-index drifts with rate but is mechanism-agnostic, supporting the claim; however the setup uses a fully synthetic Cox-exponential DGP rather than the paper's semi-synthetic real clinical datasets (PBC, FLCHAIN, METABRIC) and only two metric families.

Ranking-agreement experiments on near-tied models show oracle-ranking recovery dropping from 100% at 0% censoring to 29–42% at 80% across mechanisms (24 reps), while widely-separated models stay at 100%, directly supporting the claim's boundary; but the setup uses synthetic fixed risk scores rather than the paper's real model panel (DeepHit, NMTLR, etc.) on real datasets.

overall: The logbook runs real experiments with internally consistent numbers that support both claims—mechanism-dependent IBS distortion and ranking instability under heavy censoring for near-tied models—but on a clearly reduced fully-synthetic setup rather than the paper's semi-synthetic real-data design with its full model and metric panels.
